title: QUIC RFC 9000 NEW_CONNECTION_ID Runtime Lifecycle Topoff Work Item
summary: Complete the bounded S19P15 NEW_CONNECTION_ID runtime lifecycle proof by adding direct requirement-home coverage and correcting stale sequence handling to report RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID work instead of closing.
planned_changes:
- Keep local NEW_CONNECTION_ID issuance suppressed in zero-length local connection-ID mode.
- Add direct S19P15 requirement-home proof for zero-length-mode receive rejection, exact duplicate acceptance, sequence-based duplicate handling, and conflict rejection.
- Preserve historical peer connection-ID sequence records after active retirement.
- Treat later NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames with smaller Retire Prior To values as no-ops for the largest received threshold.
- Report a newly received sequence below the largest Retire Prior To value for one RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID emission and suppress duplicate stale retirement reports.
- Update canonical requirement trace, architecture, work-item, and verification artifacts.
verification_plan: Run the focused S19P15 runtime lifecycle requirement-home filter, regenerate the QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate canonical SpecTrace JSON, run a Release build, run the focused tests again after trace updates, and then run the full solution tests.
out_of_scope: S19P15 frame-codec field-level metadata/restructure cleanup for requirements 0002 through 0013.
Broad path migration unlinkability or preferred-address transition behavior.
New public migration APIs or route portfolio controls.
Changing congestion, PTO, or send-boundary behavior for protected RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID packet emission.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused runtime/state topoff. The S19P15-0023 fix changes below-threshold sequence receipt from a protocol violation to one-time retirement reporting; packet emission continues through the existing runtime RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID send path.
